newsitem.title: GERMANY: New approach needed on Bosnia refugees -- mediator.
newsitem.headline: New approach needed on Bosnia refugees -- mediator.

text.p: A gradual approach to getting refugees from the Bosnian civil war to go home has failed and should be replaced by a radical method involving a specific return date, a top international mediator said on Monday.

Michael Steiner, deputy to International High Representative Carl Bildt, said it might be possible to organise a mass return starting in Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation on a kind of trade-off principle.

"There has been no significant return of refugees to areas where their ethnic group is in a minority," he told a symposium in Bonn, noting that more than half of Bosnia's population did not live in their own homes.

"If as much energy were put into organising the return of refugees as has been put by the OSCE into organising elections, perhaps by having an R-Day or Return Day instead of an E-Day or Election Day, then we could achieve far more than we have with pilot projects which don't work because they lack internal balance."
The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) organised national elections in Bosnia last year and is in charge of municipal elections planned for later this year.
Steiner said "R-Day" need not be limited to a single day but could stretch over weeks.

He said there were indications that leaders of the Croat population in Bosnia were keen to stem a steady exodus of Croats from the region. He said they were increasingly ready to promote the return of Moslems and Serbs to Croat-controlled areas if this meant more Croats could go back to other areas.
Steiner said there was a growing realisation among all three ethnic groups "that Croats can only return if Moslems can return and Serbs can return, and vice versa".
"Without the return of the refugees, there will be no stable peace," he said.
